body.statement:
Let \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), put \(A=A(\eta)\), \(F_k=\operatorname{de}_{G_0(\eta)}(T_k(\eta))\cap V\), and let \(H\) be the observational skeleton.  In the causally sufficient childless-selection pre-treatment twin construction, Dai et al.'s Lemmas 3--6 give the following facts.  Observational adjacency is generated by a basal observed edge or by an observed common child that is ancestral to selection.  An observed pair is adjacent in regime \(k\) exactly when it is observationally adjacent or its endpoints are joined in \(H[A]\) by a path whose internal vertices belong to \(F_k\cap A\).  The indicator-neighbor set is
\[
\operatorname{adj}_{M_k(\eta)}(\zeta_k)\cap V
=T_k(\eta)\cup\bigl((F_k\setminus T_k(\eta))\cap A\bigr).
\]
Every indicator edge is oriented out of \(\zeta_k\).  An observed directed edge of the observational MAG is retained in the regime MAG.  For any other regime adjacency \(xy\), its marks are determined as follows: two unaffected endpoints give \(x\mathbin{-}y\); if \(y\) is affected and either \(x\) is unaffected or \(x\in\operatorname{An}_{G_0(\eta)}(y)\), the edge is \(x\to y\); the symmetric condition gives \(y\to x\); and two affected endpoints with neither ancestral to the other give \(x\leftrightarrow y\).  In particular, observational endpoints inside \(A\) are tails, and an observational adjacency meeting \(V\setminus A\) is a basal directed edge with its basal orientation.

source.verbatim_statement: Lemma 3. For any i, j ∈ [D], X_i and X_j are adjacent in M_{G^(∅)}, if and only if i and j are adjacent in G, or ch_G(i) ∩ ch_G(j) ∩ an_G(S) ≠ ∅, i.e., they involve in a same selection, or have a common child that is ancestrally selected. Lemma 4. For any i, j ∈ [D], X_i and X_j are adjacent in M_{G^(I)}, if and only if X_i and X_j are adjacent in the observational MAG M_{G^(∅)}, or there exists a path between X_i and X_j in M_{G^(∅)}, where all non-endpoint vertices are affected (i.e., in de_G(I)), and they, together with i, j, are all ancestrally selected (i.e., in an_G(S)). Lemma 5. For any j ∈ [D], ζ and X_j are adjacent in M_{G^(I)}, if and only if j is directly targeted (i.e., j ∈ I), or j is both indirectly affected and ancestrally selected (i.e., j ∈ de_G(I) ∩ an_G(S)). Lemma 6. The MAG M_{G^(I)} consists of the following edges: ‘Pseudo’ direct intervention target edges (by Lemma 5): {ζ → X_i}_{i ∈ I ∪ (de_G(I) ∩ an_G(S))}; Edges among X. Let M_G be the MAG of G over [D]. For each adjacent X_i, X_j (by Lemma 4): If i → j is in the original MAG M_G, then orient X_i → X_j in interventional MAG M_{G^(I)}; Otherwise (i.e., i — j ∈ M_G or i, j are not adjacent in M_G): If i ∉ de_G(I) and j ∉ de_G(I): orient X_i — X_j; If j ∈ de_G(I) and (i ∉ de_G(I) or i ∈ an_G(j)): orient X_i → X_j; If i ∈ de_G(I) and (j ∉ de_G(I) or j ∈ an_G(i)): orient X_j → X_i; Otherwise, i.e., both i, j ∈ de_G(I), but neither is another’s ancestor: orient X_i ↔ X_j.
